given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Two loans due 2026-03-16 are open when today is set to 2026-03-17.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs on a fresh database with no reminders.

then.why: fakeNotifications.sent must contain exactly the two reminders.
Each sent entry must carry the right memberId, loanId and dueOn.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table must hold sent_on 2026-03-17 (today) for each loan, not the due date 2026-03-16.
mutants.json lists this as covered by B3, whose test asserts that nothing is recorded on refusal.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so loan1 already has a reminder on the second run.
loan2 is returned before the job runs, while it is past its due date.
Both loans are lent on 03-02 and so are due 03-16. Both are overdue on 03-17, and no loan is within its term or due today.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (already reminded today)
then.why: After two runs sent must hold only one loan1 entry, so a duplicate send would fail.
Sent must contain only loan1, so a reminder for the returned loan2 would fail.

then.part: Sends nothing for that loan (isn't overdue)
then.why: No not-yet-overdue loan exists in the test. A change from `<` to `<=` or dropping the due check would still pass.

given.why: The fake refuses loan1 with a 503 reason.
B5 shows an unreachable API is turned into a refused result. B3's test only uses an explicit refusal.

then.why: The reminders table must hold only loan2's row.
toContainEqual checks level warn and event reminder.failed.
The fields must equal loan1's id and the exact reason string.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: The refused loan1 is the older loan, so a stop at the first failure would leave loan2 unsent and fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are processed, one of them refused.

then.why: The last log entry must have level info and event reminders.finished.
toEqual requires sent 2 and failed 1 exactly.

given.why: The tests call the client directly with a reminder.

then.why: The method, the path and the application/json content type are asserted exactly.

then.part: body `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The whole body is compared with toEqual.
202, 200 and 204 are each accepted, so a check for exactly 200 would fail.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives kind refused and a reason containing 400.

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives kind refused and a reason containing unreachable.
